$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60, one director only (Agnès Varda). Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1) with additive fields: format, tmdbYear, sightAndSound2022, rt.reason, rt.alternateCut. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (averageRating, numVotes), matched on IMDb title id; title ids found through title.crew.tsv.gz (director nconst) and cross-checked against TMDB by title, year and runtime
imdb.note: Live IMDb title pages were attempted first and did not return a usable page to an automated request (an empty response, not a human-readable page), so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead; this is the same fallback as the Kurosawa example. The dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in ESSENTIAL_10_EXAMPLE.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer (scorePercent) and critic review count (reviewCount) read from the page's embedded data
rt.note: Read directly from each film's rottentomatoes.com page with a command-line fetch, one request per page. Percentages and counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot. Where a page shows fewer than about 5 reviews no Tomatometer is published and the value is null.

sightAndSound.source: BFI, The Greatest Films of All Time (2022 Sight and Sound poll), positions as listed on the page
sightAndSound.note: The page text was read in two halves; ranks 49-50 and the very bottom of the list were not visible in the extracted text. A film shown without a position was not seen in the portions read; that is not proof it is absent. '=' marks a tie. The page does not state 'critics' poll' in the extracted text, so the figure is labelled 'the 2022 Sight and Sound poll'.

films.title: The Beaches of Agnès
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer). Documentary (autobiographical essay).
films.rationale: A self-portrait told through mirrors, beaches and staged memories; the highest IMDb rating in the nine (8.0, from 5,463 votes), with 97% from 71 RT reviews.

films.title: Faces Places
films.directorCreditNote: Co-directed: TMDB lists JR (person 226050) as a second director. Credited as director in the TMDB Directing section and on the film page (roles shown: Director, Writer). Documentary, co-directed with the artist JR (TMDB person 226050). TMDB, IMDb and RT all list both directors. Flagged: a joint credit.
films.rationale: A road film in which Varda and JR paste portraits on village walls; Oscar-nominated for Best Documentary Feature and the strongest critic result of the list (99% from 143 reviews).

films.title: Vagabond
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: A young drifter's last weeks reconstructed from the testimony of people who met her; Golden Lion at Venice 1985 and 100% from 26 RT reviews.

films.title: Daguerréotypes
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer). Documentary. Year conflict: TMDB 1978, RT 1976, IMDb 1975.

rt.rtYearNote: RT page shows 1976 (US or festival release year); the ledger uses the original release year.

films.rationale: A portrait of the shopkeepers on her own street, Rue Daguerre; the template for the observational documentary mode she returned to for forty years. Evidence is thin (2,362 IMDb votes, 11 RT reviews).

films.title: Cléo from 5 to 7
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: A singer awaits a medical result across ninety minutes of Paris afternoon, in near real time; the highest-placed Varda in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll (14th) and her most-watched film on IMDb (32,645 votes).

films.title: The Gleaners and I
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer). Documentary.
films.rationale: A documentary essay on foragers and waste that made her own filming a subject; =67 in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll and 95% from 44 RT reviews.

films.title: Le Bonheur
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).

rt.rtYearNote: RT shows 88% from only 8 reviews: thin.

films.rationale: A sunlit story of a happy marriage that turns disturbing by form alone; =152 in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll and the best-known of her 1960s fiction after Cléo.

films.title: One Sings, the Other Doesn't
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: Two women's friendship over some fifteen years, linked to the women's movement and abortion rights; the clearest statement of her political fiction, though only 65% on RT.

films.title: La Pointe Courte
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).

rt.rtYearNote: RT shows 4 reviews and no Tomatometer yet. TMDB and RT list 1956; IMDb and the roster proposal list 1955.
rt.reason: RT has not published a Tomatometer for this page (only 4 reviews read).

films.rationale: Her debut, a married couple's quarrel set against a fishing village, edited by Alain Resnais and widely seen as an advance sign of the French New Wave.

nearMisses.title: Varda by Agnès
nearMisses.reason: Her final self-portrait (RT 98% from 91 reviews), but IMDb files it as a miniseries (tt9530198; 7.8 from 2,872 votes, with a separate tt43684922 entry), so the figures cannot be cleanly tied to the film; first reserve.

nearMisses.title: Jacquot de Nantes
nearMisses.reason: Tribute to Jacques Demy; IMDb 7.6 from 2,413 votes, RT 83% from 6 reviews.

nearMisses.title: Kung-Fu Master!
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 6.9 from 2,598 votes; RT 100% from 7 reviews.

nearMisses.title: Documenteur
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 6.9 from 1,539 votes; RT has 2 reviews.

nearMisses.title: Mur Murs
nearMisses.reason: Documentary on Los Angeles murals; IMDb 7.4 from 1,377 votes.

unverified: Four of the nine are documentaries and one is co-directed; this matches the owner's decision to include them where essential.
La Pointe Courte is dated 1955 (festival and IMDb) here, 1956 on TMDB and RT. Daguerréotypes is dated 1975 here; TMDB gives 1978, RT 1976.
La Pointe Courte has no Tomatometer on RT (4 reviews): null with reason, not zero.

Varda by Agnès (2019) could not be cleanly tied to an IMDb feature entry (IMDb lists it as a miniseries, tt9530198, 7.8 from 2,872 votes, plus a separate tt43684922 'Causerie' entry), so it is a reserve rather than a ranked film.
The IMDb dataset marks The Gleaners and I as the 2000 film; the two-years-later follow-up (TMDB 84026) is a separate short film.
